newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch state demand raises bottom guilder - rates.
newsitem.headline: Dutch state demand raises bottom guilder - rates.

text.p: Dutch money rates rose some more basis points on Wednesday and call money was under upward pressure while the Dutch state was searching for liquidity, mainly through its Dutch Treasury Certificates (DTCs) programme.
"The rates for DTCs has risen substantially in the last few weeks," said one dealer, adding this had dragged up money market rates as well.
"Investors had stayed somewhat sidelined when the Dutch state brought its DTCs into the market," said one dealer, adding this attitude had paid off and the rate for DTCs had risen.
At the start of the latest DTC programme (for January, February and March) the rate for DTCs was 2.75/2.80, dealers said.
"Four weeks later the rate for the January programme has - step by step - risen to 2.91 percent, for February to 2.93 and for March to 2.94," said another dealer.
Dealers said business in DTCs had been substantial as result of the higher rate. "Better than before I think," said one.
The approaching year end had also pushed money market rates up, dealers said. Most trade was in short-dated deposits and call money.
"Why invest in one-month deposits if the return on one week paper is higher," said one.
One-week deposits were trading at 2.90 percent bid and one-month paper was bid at 2.86 percent.

The rate for call money had been volatile earlier during today's session, said one dealer, but in the beginning of the afternoon call slipped back to near Tuesday's levels, trading at 2.87/93 percent bid from 2.87 percent on Tuesday.
Dealers were convinced that the Dutch central bank would set an unchanged advances pact this afternoon, which was currently pegged at 2.50 percent.
The guilder was glued to yesterday's level, trading at 112.175 per 100 marks.
